# `voxel/VoxelRaycast.js`

> **Source:** `engine/voxel/VoxelRaycast.js`

VoxelRaycast.js - Amanatides & Woo DDA Voxel Ray Traversal Based on "A Fast Voxel Traversal Algorithm for Ray Tracing" (1987) Features: - CPU DDA for single raycasts (picking, quick LOS) - GPU compute shader for batch raycasts (AI mass LOS checks) - Block picking with face normal detection - Line-of-sight with early termination - Configurable solid/transparent material checks Performance: - CPU: O(n) where n = voxels crossed (typically 10-100 for gameplay ranges) - GPU: Parallel processing of 1000+ rays per dispatch

## Classes

### `class VoxelRaycastGPU`

GPU-accelerated batch voxel raycasting system Use when processing 100+ rays per frame

| `raycastBatch` | `async raycastBatch(rays, loadedChunks)` | Perform batch raycast |
| `destroy` | `destroy()` | Cleanup GPU resources |

## Functions

### `raycastVoxels(origin, direction, getVoxel, options = {})`

Raycast through voxel world using DDA algorithm Returns first solid voxel hit along ray

**Parameters:**

- `origin` *(number[])* — [x, y, z] ray origin in world coords
- `direction` *(number[])* — [x, y, z] normalized direction
- `getVoxel` *(Function)* — (x, y, z) => material ID or null if unloaded
- `options` *(Object)* — Raycast options
- `options.maxDistance` *(number)* — Maximum ray distance (default 100)
- `options.isSolid` *(Function)* — (material) => boolean (default: !== AIR)
- `options.ignoreMaterials` *(Set)* — Materials to treat as transparent

**Returns:** {position, normal, distance, material, voxelCoord} or null

### `hasVoxelLineOfSight(from, to, getVoxel, options = {})`

Check line of sight between two points through voxels Returns true if no solid voxels block the path

**Parameters:**

- `from` *(number[])* — [x, y, z] start position
- `to` *(number[])* — [x, y, z] end position
- `getVoxel` *(Function)* — (x, y, z) => material ID
- `options` *(Object)* — Same as raycastVoxels

**Returns:** True if line of sight is clear

### `pickBlock(origin, direction, getVoxel, maxDistance = 10)`

Block picking - raycast from camera with face/placement info Returns both the hit block and the adjacent empty block for placement

**Parameters:**

- `origin` *(number[])* — Camera/eye position
- `direction` *(number[])* — Look direction (normalized)
- `getVoxel` *(Function)* — (x, y, z) => material ID
- `maxDistance` *(number)* — Max pick distance (default 10)

**Returns:** {block: voxelCoord, face: normal, placeAt: voxelCoord, distance}

### `traceVoxelPath(origin, direction, getVoxel, maxDistance = 50, options = {})`

Trace ray through voxels collecting all intersected voxels Useful for beam weapons, explosion rays, etc.

**Parameters:**

- `origin` *(number[])* — Ray origin
- `direction` *(number[])* — Normalized direction
- `getVoxel` *(Function)* — (x, y, z) => material ID
- `maxDistance` *(number)* — Max trace distance
- `options` *(Object)* — Additional options

**Returns:** Array of {voxelCoord, material, distance, entryPoint}

### `computePixelToRayMatrix(cameraPos, cameraRotation, fovRad, screenWidth, screenHeight)`

Compute a single matrix that transforms screen pixel coords to world-space ray directions. This avoids per-pixel matrix multiplications in shaders. Usage: rayDir = normalize((pixelToRay * vec4(pixelX, pixelY, 1, 1)).xyz - cameraPos)

**Parameters:**

- `cameraPos` *(number[])* — Camera world position [x, y, z]
- `cameraRotation` *(number[])* — Euler angles [pitch, yaw, roll] in radians
- `fovRad` *(number)* — Field of view in radians
- `screenWidth` *(number)* — Screen width in pixels
- `screenHeight` *(number)* — Screen height in pixels

**Returns:** 4x4 matrix (column-major)

### `screenPixelToRay(pixelX, pixelY, pixelToRay, cameraPos)`

Generate ray from screen pixel using precomputed pixel-to-ray matrix

**Parameters:**

- `pixelX` *(number)* — Screen X coordinate
- `pixelY` *(number)* — Screen Y coordinate
- `pixelToRay` *(Float32Array)* — 4x4 matrix from computePixelToRayMatrix
- `cameraPos` *(number[])* — Camera position for ray origin

**Returns:** {origin, direction}

Convert step count to heat map color (inferno palette)

### `triangleVoxelIntersect(a, b, c, voxelMin, voxelMax)`

Check if a triangle intersects a voxel using separating axis theorem. Based on DeadlockCode's implementation.

**Parameters:**

- `a` *(number[])* — Triangle vertex A [x, y, z]
- `b` *(number[])* — Triangle vertex B [x, y, z]
- `c` *(number[])* — Triangle vertex C [x, y, z]
- `voxelMin` *(number[])* — Voxel minimum corner [x, y, z]
- `voxelMax` *(number[])* — Voxel maximum corner [x, y, z]

**Returns:** True if triangle intersects voxel

### `voxelizeMesh(vertices, triangles, resolution, boundsMin, boundsMax)`

Voxelize a triangle mesh into a voxel grid

**Parameters:**

- `vertices` *(Array)* — Array of [x, y, z] vertices
- `triangles` *(Array)* — Array of [i0, i1, i2] index triplets
- `resolution` *(number)* — Grid resolution per axis
- `boundsMin` *(number[])* — Bounding box minimum
- `boundsMax` *(number[])* — Bounding box maximum

**Returns:** Voxel grid (1 = solid, 0 = empty)

## Notes & Examples

### Voxel World System

The voxel system provides chunked 3D grids with fast access, mesh generation, and level-of-detail (LOD). Chunks are 32³ by default and stream in/out based on camera position. The mesher generates greedy or marching-cubes geometry depending on material.

**Example: Creating and modifying a voxel world**
```js
import { VoxelWorld } from 'engine/voxel/VoxelWorld.js';
import { VoxelMesher } from 'engine/voxel/VoxelMesher.js';

const world = new VoxelWorld({
  chunkSize: 32,
  loadDistance: 8  // chunks
});

// Set voxel at world position
world.setVoxel(10, 5, 10, {
  type: 'grass',
  color: [0.2, 0.7, 0.1]
});

world.setVoxel(10, 4, 10, { type: 'dirt' });

// Generate mesh for rendering
const mesher = new VoxelMesher(world);
const geometry = mesher.generateChunk(0, 0, 0);

// Raycast to find clicked voxel
const hit = world.raycast(rayOrigin, rayDir, 100);
if (hit) {
  world.setVoxel(hit.x, hit.y, hit.z, null);  // Remove
}
```
